learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: What does Penelope use to test Odysseus?
Use the cited passage to explain: Why is the bed a strong recognition test?

main.author: Homer
main.locator: Book 23, Odysseus explains the rooted bed; local text file lines 10218-10223 (physical file lines, not ancient verse numbers)
main.excerpt: There was a young olive growing within the precincts of the house, in full vigour, and about as thick as a bearing-post. I built my room round this with strong walls of stone and a roof to cover them, and I made the doors strong and well-fitting. Then I cut off the top boughs of the olive tree and left the stump standing.
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Penelope does not accept the stranger’s identity on appearance alone. Her instruction about moving their bed draws out knowledge of its construction around a rooted olive tree: a private, shared history becomes evidence of identity.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “There was a young olive growing within the precincts of the house, in full vigour, and about as thick as a bearing-post. I built my room round this with strong walls of stone and a roof to cover them, and I made the doors strong and well-fitting. Then I cut off the top boughs of the olive tree and left the stump standing.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Identity in the Odyssey is proved relationally. The hero must be recognized by the people and places that can still read him correctly.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Penelope’s test asks for private knowledge, not another boast of heroic achievement. The rooted bed connects identity with the particular household to which Odysseus is returning.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: The final heroic skill is patience after arrival, when revenge is available but restoration is not yet complete.

quiz.prompt: Why is the bed a strong recognition test?

choices.text: Athena has written Odysseus’ name on it.
Its construction is knowledge shared within their marriage.
Every visitor to Ithaca has seen it moved.
